findings.title: Same NPE remains in the other getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: The PR fixes only getSubGroupsCount(). The three getSubGroupsStream(...) overloads (lines 256, 262, 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` with no null check. `modelSupplier.get()` returns null when the group was deleted concurrently, which is the exact condition behind #40368. Concurrent deletion of a group that is being listed or expanded can therefore still throw an NPE on these paths. A related path, `isUpdated()` (lines 73-74), throws IllegalStateException when the group disappears after invalidation. The fix is therefore partial, and the new null-tolerance applies to one method only.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() now silently returns null for a deleted group
findings.body: When the underlying group no longer exists, getSubGroupsCount() returns null instead of signalling that the group is gone. The JPA implementation of GroupModel never returns null here. Callers that unbox the Long, or that treat a missing count as 0, will still fail or misreport. In `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` the deleted group is still emitted in the response with a null subGroupCount, rather than being skipped. This hides the race instead of handling it, and the nullable return is not documented in the GroupModel contract.

findings.title: Concurrency test starts an unjoined reader thread and may not detect the failure
findings.body: The reader thread is started with `new Thread(...).start()` and is never joined or awaited. After `deletedAll.set(true)` the test immediately asserts on `caughtExceptions`. The reader may be mid-request at that point, so an exception it throws afterwards is lost, and the thread can outlive the test while still hitting the server. The test also does not wait for the reader to start before deleting, and it has no timeout or deterministic ordering. It is probabilistic: it may pass on unfixed code if deletion finishes before the reader overlaps, and it can leak a thread into later tests. Use an ExecutorService or a joined thread with a start latch, and assert only after the reader has fully stopped.
